newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Brussels bourse stalls on nerves and no news.
newsitem.headline: Brussels bourse stalls on nerves and no news.

text.p: The Brussels bourse slid gently into the red on an uninspired Thursday as bond yields rose and New York drifted down, and traders said players were becoming increasingly nervous at these rarified levels.

"The market still wants to go up, but we are now at levels where nervousness is natural," one trader said. "Everybody wants to make sure their profits are safe. The higher we go the more nervous people will become."
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares ended 2.29 points or 0.10 percent down at 2,245.54 in a 2,252.58/2,237.94 range with some 2.6 billion francs of Belgian shares traded.
Broad-based holding company Ackermans was the star of the market, rising 5.5 percent to 7,300 francs -- although traders were at a loss to explain the reason.
One speculated that it was due to players belatedly latching on to forecasts for a strong performance by the company's dredging subsidiary this year.
"The market is still eager for buying opportunities and sometimes reacts unexpectedly to old news," he said.
The same seemed to be true of film finisher Spector which rose 2.8 percent to 2,560 francs. The firm made positive noises at its annual meeting last week.
Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere dropped 1.9 percent to 2,825 francs.
Traders said it was mainly due to comments on Wednesday at parent company SGB's annual meeting that indicated the firm was not up for sale despite the fact that it was not a strategic holding.
"Some people had been hoping for a sale, so now the speculative premium is coming out of the share," one trader said.
Kredietbank gained 0.55 percent to 13,750 francs on renewed speculation of possible strategic cooperations.
